_meta.description: Curated paper index for awesome-reasoning-models-theory. Each entry: id, title, authors, year, venue, url, chapter, type, status, tldr.

status_legend.verified: Read, summary verified against the source

papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.authors: Wei, Wang, Schuurmans, Bosma, Ichter, Xia, Chi, Le, Zhou
papers.tldr: Letting models emit intermediate steps unlocks multi-step reasoning at sufficient scale. The seed paper of the CoT era.

papers.title: Show Your Work: Scratchpads for Intermediate Computation with Language Models
papers.authors: Nye, Andreassen, Gur-Ari, Michalewski, Austin, Bieber, Dohan, Lewkowycz, Bosma, Luan, Sutton, Odena
papers.tldr: Original 'scratchpad' framing. Predates Wei et al. by months; the term survives in the learnability literature.

papers.title: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners
papers.tldr: 'Let's think step by step' alone elicits CoT, no exemplars needed. The zero-shot CoT result.

papers.title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think
papers.tldr: Bias the input, the model's CoT will rationalize the biased answer. The seminal unfaithfulness demonstration.

papers.title: Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
papers.authors: Lanham, Chen, Radhakrishnan, Steiner, Denison, Hernandez, Li, Durmus, Hubinger, Kernion, Lukosiute, Nguyen, Cheng, Joseph, Showk, Bai, Chen, Conerly, DasSarma, Drain, Fort, Ganguli, Hatfield-Dodds, Henighan, Johnston, Mann, Nanda, Olsson, Amodei, Brown, Kaplan, McCandlish, Olah, Schiefer, Perez
papers.tldr: Operationalize faithfulness via truncation, paraphrase, and step-injection tests. Larger ≠ more faithful.

papers.title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally Can Be More Effective Than Scaling Model Parameters
papers.tldr: At fixed FLOPs, optimally-allocated test-time compute can match or beat 14× larger models on math. The headline TTC paper.

papers.title: Learning to Reason with LLMs (o1 announcement)
papers.tldr: OpenAI's o1 announcement. Plot showing accuracy increasing with both train- and test-time compute became the era's defining figure.

papers.title: s1: Simple Test-Time Scaling
papers.authors: Muennighoff, Yang, Shi, Li, Fei-Fei, Hajishirzi, Zettlemoyer, Liang, Candès, Hashimoto
papers.tldr: Just SFT on 1k curated traces + budget-forcing at inference reaches strong AIME numbers. Argues TTC is largely a budgeting trick.

papers.title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
papers.authors: Wang, Wei, Schuurmans, Le, Chi, Narang, Chowdhery, Zhou
papers.tldr: Sample K chains, take majority vote on the answer. Cheap, no verifier, and strong baseline.

papers.title: Let's Verify Step by Step
papers.authors: Lightman, Kosaraju, Burda, Edwards, Baker, Lee, Leike, Schulman, Sutskever, Cobbe
papers.tldr: Process reward models (step-graded) train better verifiers than outcome reward models, even at equal label budget.

papers.title: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems
papers.authors: Cobbe, Kosaraju, Bavarian, Chen, Jun, Kaiser, Plappert, Tworek, Hilton, Nakano, Hesse, Schulman
papers.tldr: Introduces GSM8K and the verifier-reranking idea. Pre-PRM, but the same recipe.

papers.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
papers.authors: Yao, Yu, Zhao, Shafran, Griffiths, Cao, Narasimhan
papers.tldr: Treat CoT generation as tree search with a self-rated value function. Generalizes self-consistency to tree topologies.

papers.title: Graph of Thoughts: Solving Elaborate Problems with Large Language Models
papers.authors: Besta, Blach, Kubicek, Gerstenberger, Podstawski, Gianinazzi, Gajda, Lehmann, Niewiadomski, Nyczyk, Hoefler
papers.tldr: Generalizes ToT to DAGs with explicit aggregation operators. More expressive, more compute.

papers.title: Recursive Self-Aggregation Unlocks Deep Thinking in Large Language Models
papers.authors: Venkatraman, Liu, Cherian, Mottaghi, Ren, Schroers, Smith, Wang, Yan
papers.tldr: Sample K chains, summarize into a new prompt, recurse. Trades branching for depth at inference.

papers.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
papers.authors: Shao, Wang, Zhu, Xu, Song, Bi, Zhang, Zhang, Li, Wu, Guo
papers.tldr: Origin of GRPO: group-relative advantage, no value head. The algorithmic predecessor to R1.

papers.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: R1-Zero (pure RL from base) and R1 (SFT cold-start + RL refinement). The defining paper of the era.

papers.title: Tülu 3: Pushing Frontiers in Open Language Model Post-Training
papers.authors: Lambert, Morrison, Pyatkin, Huang, Ivison, Brahman, Miranda, Liu, Dziri, Lyu, Gu, Malik, Graf, Hwang, Yang, Bras, Tafjord, Wilhelm, Soldaini, Smith, Wang, Dasigi, Hajishirzi
papers.tldr: Names and demonstrates RLVR (RL from Verifiable Rewards) at scale. Concurrent with R1's research.

papers.title: ReFT: Reasoning with Reinforced Fine-Tuning
papers.authors: Luong, Zhang, Nguyen, Cai, Yang, Vu
papers.tldr: SFT-then-PPO on math. Pre-R1 evidence that policy-gradient on outcome reward improves chain quality.

papers.title: Stream of Search (SoS): Learning to Search in Language
papers.tldr: Train models on synthetic search traces so the search loop is internalized at inference. Pre-R1 'search-as-a-skill' result.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
papers.tldr: Push RL too hard against a learned reward, the policy diverges from the true objective. Predicts the inverse-U with KL.

papers.title: Do Not Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs
papers.authors: Chen, Xu, Arcuschin, Geva, Gandelsman, Belrose, Beren, Wattenberg
papers.tldr: On trivial questions, o1-like models emit hundreds of tokens of self-doubt and reach lower accuracy. Names overthinking.

papers.title: Don't Overthink It: Preferring Shorter Thinking Chains for Improved LLM Reasoning
papers.tldr: Shorter CoT often beats longer CoT at fixed budget. Best-of-N with length-penalized reranking.

papers.title: Towards Thinking-Optimal Scaling of Test-Time Compute for LLM Reasoning
papers.tldr: Per-task optimal CoT length exists. Beyond it, accuracy degrades. Argues for adaptive budgets, not maximal ones.

papers.title: The Expressive Power of Transformers with Chain of Thought
papers.tldr: Polynomial-step CoT lifts log-precision transformers from TC⁰ to P. Formal compute-depth equivalence.

papers.title: Towards Revealing the Mystery behind Chain of Thought: A Theoretical Perspective
papers.authors: Feng, Tang, Liu, Zhang, Chen, Wang, Wang, Yang
papers.tldr: CoT lets a constant-depth transformer approximate any polynomial-time Turing machine. Sister of Merrill–Sabharwal.

papers.title: Chain of Thought Empowers Transformers to Solve Inherently Serial Problems
papers.tldr: Constant-depth transformers without CoT cannot solve some serial problems; with CoT they can. Tightens the formal account.

papers.title: An Explanation of In-Context Learning as Implicit Bayesian Inference
papers.tldr: ICL = implicit Bayes over latent concepts. Often extended to motivate the 'CoT as posterior over solution programs' account.

papers.title: The Pitfalls of Next-Token Prediction
papers.tldr: Teacher-forced learners exploit shortcuts ('Clever Hans'). Argues against naive autoregressive training as a path to robust reasoning.

papers.title: Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think
papers.tldr: Even reasoning-RL-trained models often fail to mention hints used to reach an answer. The 2025 update of Turpin et al.

papers.title: Taming Imperfect Process Verifiers: A Sampling Perspective
papers.tldr: Theoretical bounds on how an imperfect PRM should be used in tree search. Cleans up an under-analyzed corner.

papers.title: QwQ: Reflect Deeply on the Boundaries of the Unknown (technical preview)
papers.tldr: Qwen's reasoning preview. Open-weights long-CoT reasoner reaching strong math/code numbers; predates R1's recipe by weeks.

papers.title: Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Claude Code (extended thinking)
papers.tldr: Anthropic's extended-thinking mode shipped to production. Configurable token budget, integrated with code agent.

papers.title: AI achieves silver-medal standard solving International Mathematical Olympiad problems
papers.tldr: AlphaProof + AlphaGeometry 2 hits IMO silver. Heavy structured search, Lean proof verifier in the loop.

papers.title: Gemini Deep Think achieves IMO gold-medal standard
papers.tldr: Gemini Deep Think reaches IMO gold. Heavy parallel sampling + verification at inference; recipe partially disclosed.

papers.title: GPQA: A Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark
papers.authors: Rein, Hou, Stickland, Petty, Pang, Dirani, Michael, Bowman
papers.tldr: PhD-level science MCQ that survived the 2024-25 saturation wave. The 'Diamond' subset is the standard hard slice.

papers.title: FrontierMath: A Benchmark for Evaluating Advanced Mathematical Reasoning in AI
papers.authors: Glazer, Erdil, Besiroglu, Chen, Ho, Ramirez, Schwarting, Stuart, Heimersheim, Cohen, Niu, Zhao, Tsoukalas, Bostrom, Kerr, Tang, et al.
papers.tldr: Original research-level math problems, expert-curated to resist contamination. Single-digit % even for frontier reasoners.

papers.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
papers.authors: Jimenez, Yang, Wettig, Yao, Pei, Press, Narasimhan
papers.tldr: Real GitHub issues with known passing patches. The 'Verified' subset is the human-validated standard.

papers.title: ARC Prize: Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus
papers.tldr: Visual abstraction tasks designed to be hard for memorization-heavy LLMs. ARC-AGI-2 (2024) and ARC-AGI-3 (2026) are the active tracks.

papers.title: RL is the new pretraining (Interconnects)
papers.tldr: Frames RLVR as the new compute-allocation target, replacing next-token loss as the dominant pretraining objective.

papers.title: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
papers.authors: Ouyang, Wu, Jiang, Almeida, Wainwright, Mishkin, Zhang, Agarwal, Slama, Ray, et al.
papers.tldr: InstructGPT — RLHF on GPT-3. Predecessor of the alignment era; conceptual base from which RLVR diverged.

papers.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
papers.authors: Rafailov, Sharma, Mitchell, Ermon, Manning, Finn
papers.tldr: Closed-form RL-free preference optimization. Mostly displaced by RLVR for verifiable tasks.

papers.title: The Parallelism Tradeoff: Limitations of Log-Precision Transformers
papers.tldr: Log-precision transformers without CoT live in TC⁰. The lower bound that motivates compute-depth extension via CoT.

papers.title: Language Models Are Greedy Reasoners: A Systematic Formal Analysis of Chain-of-Thought
papers.tldr: Pre-RL-era audit of CoT failure modes on synthetic logical inference. Documents the greedy-shortcut tendency.

papers.title: The N+ Implementation Details of RLHF / RLVR (TRL series)
papers.tldr: The unglamorous gotchas: KL targeting, advantage normalization, value clipping, off-policy correction. Saves weeks of debugging.

papers.title: Open-Reasoner-Zero: An Open Source Approach to Scaling Up RL on Base Models
papers.authors: Hu, Zhao, Zhang, Wei, Li, Chen, Li, Zheng, Chen, Yang, Zhang, Yang, Han, Tu
papers.tldr: Open R1-Zero-style RL recipe on Qwen-base. One of the cluster of mid-2025 reproductions establishing the recipe is portable.

papers.title: SimpleRL: Reproducing R1-Zero on a Single Node
papers.tldr: Minimal R1-Zero-style reproduction. Single-node, ~hours to see the signal. Most-cited tutorial reimplementation.

papers.title: verl: Volcano Engine Reinforcement Learning for LLMs
papers.tldr: Production-grade RL framework for LLMs. PPO, GRPO, REINFORCE++ implementations; standard for serious R1 reproductions.

papers.title: Recursive Introspection: Teaching Language Model Agents How to Self-Improve
papers.authors: Qu, Zhang, Pal, Mitchell, Tucker, Zhao, Lin, Hu, Stefankovic, Chi
papers.tldr: Train models to improve their own answers iteratively. Pre-R1 evidence that self-correction is RL-trainable.

papers.title: Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Kumar, Zhuang, Agarwal, Su, Co-Reyes, Singh, Baumli, Iqbal, Bishop, Roelofs, Zhang, McKinney, Shrivastava, Paduraru, Tucker, Precup, Behbahani, Faust
papers.tldr: SCoRe — multi-turn RL for self-correction. Important precursor to the R1-style 'aha moment' phenomenon.

papers.title: Teaching Large Language Models to Reason with Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Havrilla, Du, Raparthy, Nalmpantis, Dwivedi-Yu, Zhuravinskyi, Hambro, Sukhbaatar, Raileanu
papers.tldr: Compares Expert Iteration, PPO, REINFORCE-Leave-One-Out for reasoning. Surprising result: simpler often beats PPO.

papers.title: Solving Math Word Problems with Process- and Outcome-Based Feedback
papers.authors: Uesato, Kushman, Kumar, Song, Siegel, Wang, Creswell, Irving, Higgins
papers.tldr: Pre-Lightman work showing process feedback helps. The earliest PRM-vs-ORM comparison at scale.

papers.title: Math-Shepherd: Verify and Reinforce LLMs Step-by-Step without Human Annotations
papers.authors: Wang, Li, Shao, Xu, Dai, Li, Chen, Wu, Sui
papers.tldr: Auto-PRM via Monte-Carlo rollout. Replaces expensive step-level human labels; near-PRM quality at scale.

papers.title: Selection-Inference: Exploiting Large Language Models for Interpretable Logical Reasoning
papers.tldr: Decompose CoT into select-then-infer steps with explicit verification. Pre-ToT explicit-step search.

papers.title: Decomposed Prompting: A Modular Approach for Solving Complex Tasks
papers.authors: Khot, Trivedi, Finlayson, Fu, Richardson, Clark, Sabharwal
papers.tldr: Programmatic decomposition of CoT into typed sub-tasks dispatched to specialist prompts. Search topology made explicit.

papers.title: Scaling Test-Time Compute via Search Against Weaker Verifiers
papers.tldr: How verifier quality interacts with sampling budget. Establishes when more samples helps and when it hurts.

papers.title: OpenAI o1 System Card
papers.tldr: Official system card. Discusses CoT-based oversight and the 'don't show users the reasoning trace' policy decision.

papers.title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
papers.authors: Sharma, Tong, Korbak, Duvenaud, Askell, Bowman, Cheng, Durmus, Hatfield-Dodds, Johnston, Kravec, Maxwell, McCandlish, Ndousse, Rausch, Schiefer, Yan, Zhang, Perez
papers.tldr: Models reshape their stated reasoning toward what users seem to want. Adjacent to the unfaithfulness literature.

papers.title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
papers.authors: Hubinger, Denison, Mu, Lambert, Tong, MacDiarmid, Lanham, Ziegler, Maxwell, Cheng, Jermyn, Schiefer, Mishra, Mazeika, Mears, Phuong, Drain, Abramowitz, Cohen, Petruska, Lhoest, Bills, Jiang, Cheng, Chen, Joseph, Olsson, Bai, Mann, Henighan, Hatfield-Dodds, Hatfield-Dodds, Showk, Showk, Bills, Cohen, Eydun, Joseph, Olsson, Catt, Olsson, Brown, Ndousse, Sully, Joseph, Sully, Olsson, Ndousse, Sully, Brown, Olsson, Sully, Ndousse, Olsson, Olsson, Sully, Brown, Hubinger, Perez
papers.tldr: Trained-in deceptive behaviors persist through safety training. Adjacent to faithfulness: behaviors and reported reasoning can diverge by design.

papers.title: Towards a Theoretical Understanding of Two-Stage Training of Reasoning Models
papers.authors: Various 2025-2026 follow-ups (placeholder for the SFT+RL theory cluster)
papers.tldr: Cluster of 2025-26 theory papers on why SFT-then-RL works for reasoning. Several candidate explanations under active debate.

papers.title: DeepSeek-R1-Distill: Distilling Reasoning to Smaller Open Models
papers.tldr: Distill R1's chains into Qwen-7B/14B/32B and Llama-8B/70B students. Per-parameter, more effective than RLVR-on-the-small-model.

papers.title: Tracing the Thoughts of a Large Language Model
papers.tldr: Circuits-level evidence that planning happens before generation. Concrete cases where the visible chain isn't the computation.
